about.heading: From Computational Physics to Production AI
paragraphs: I'm an AI engineer with a Computational Physics background, which means linear algebra, probability, optimisation and numerical methods are working tools rather than something I outsource to a framework. It's how I decide what a problem actually needs before reaching for a library.

That shows in the work: fine-tuning LLaMA 3.2 with Unsloth instead of prompting around a weak base model, hybrid SQL and vector retrieval instead of a default RAG template, and multi-agent graphs where the control flow is designed rather than hoped for.
The research side is published. A comparative study of LSTM and Quantum LSTM for stock market movement (arXiv), which grew out of my Computational Physics thesis.

The other half is shipping. Over 4+ years I've delivered SaaS and micro-SaaS products with authentication, payments, background workers, CI/CD and cloud deployment, 25+ AI systems in production for more than 100 clients across healthcare, real estate, e-commerce and finance.

I lean on modern AI tooling day to day, Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, because leverage is the point. It's how one engineer covers architecture, training, backend, frontend and deployment on the same project without it showing in the result.
highlights: Trains and fine-tunes models, not just API calls

approach.label: How I Work
approach.heading: Depth Where It Matters, Shipped End to End
approach.intro: AI projects usually fail at one of two ends: the model was picked without understanding it, or it never made it out of the notebook. I cover both.

pillars.title: The mathematics, not just the API
pillars.body: A Computational Physics degree means linear algebra, probability, optimisation and numerical methods are working tools. I pick an architecture because the problem calls for it, and when training stops converging I can reason about why instead of swapping libraries.
pillars.proof: Published on arXiv: LSTM vs. Quantum LSTM for stock market movement
pillars.formulaCaption: the update rule under every training loop

pillars.title: Built from scratch when it should be
pillars.body: Fine-tuning LLaMA 3.2 with Unsloth rather than prompting around a weak base model. Hybrid SQL and vector retrieval rather than a default RAG template. Agent graphs with deliberate control flow rather than hoping the model plans well on its own.
pillars.proof: LLaMA 3.2 fine-tuning · FAISS, Chroma, Pinecone · LangGraph multi-agent systems
pillars.formulaCaption: cosine similarity, the core of every retrieval step

pillars.title: Products, not scripts
pillars.body: A model behind an endpoint is not a product. What I hand over includes authentication, payments, background workers, error handling, CI/CD, deployment and a frontend a paying customer can use on day one.
pillars.proof: SaaS and micro-SaaS delivered with Django, FastAPI, Celery, Docker and GitHub Actions
pillars.formulaCaption: the numbers a production service is judged on

pillars.title: Automation as leverage
pillars.body: Pipelines that remove the manual step rather than shortening it, plus heavy use of modern AI tooling in my own workflow. That leverage is how one engineer owns architecture, training, backend, frontend and deployment on the same project.
pillars.proof: 40 to 70% average cost reduction on the workflows I automate
pillars.formulaCaption: what you optimise when inference bills scale

pillars.title: Measured, not vibed
pillars.body: "It seems to work" is not a launch criterion. Every pipeline ships with an evaluation set, a regression suite over prompts and retrieval, and a number attached, so a change that quietly makes answers worse gets caught before your users find it.
pillars.proof: Held-out eval sets · retrieval and answer scoring · regression runs in CI
pillars.formulaCaption: precision and recall, before anything goes live

pillars.title: Your data stays yours
pillars.body: Healthcare records, claims and financial filings do not belong in someone else's training set. Sensitive fields get redacted before they reach a model, and where the data cannot leave the building I run open-weight models on your own infrastructure instead.
pillars.proof: PII redaction · self-hosted LLaMA and open-weight models · scoped access control
pillars.formulaCaption: the order that keeps raw identifiers out of a vector store
